solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: New app isn't ready to be given fresh colour scheme?

definitions.note: a past participle: the question mark admits a spray job is only one way of recolouring

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A fresh phone application is not yet ready to be released with its new colour scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New app' reads as software, but 'New' signals the rearrangement of APP ISN'T READY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something coated afresh from an aerosol can has literally been recoloured, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Big match is fun: I clap wildly

indicators.note: wildly says these letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A spectator enjoying a major game applauds enthusiastically.
explanation.definitionFit: The final of a knockout trophy competition, such as the FA's, is the season's biggest football fixture.

clue.text: A duck of note turning up in Australia

indicators.note: in puts the note inside the abbreviation for Australia
in a down clue, up means the word for Australia is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Oz is the informal name for Australia

indicators.note: turning means the note is turned round, so its two letters are read backwards

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A notable failure by a batsman happening in an Australian cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' really flips the whole of the note-inside-Australia at once; flipping each piece and then nesting gives the same letters. In cricket a duck is a batsman's score of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a duck means a score of nil, the figure nought.

clue.text: Military display rubbish also

parts.note: tat is cheap worthless stuff
too means as well

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a parade of soldiers as rubbish as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Edinburgh's famous evening show of military bands and drill is called by this name.

clue.text: Relentlessly pursue setter maybe for fifties record

parts.note: to hound someone is to chase them without letting up
a setter is a breed of dog, a gundog

explanation.surface: Someone harasses a crossword compiler, perhaps over an old 1950s record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the crossword compiler but is the gundog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley's 1956 hit single bears this title, so it is a famous record of that decade.

clue.text: City of Helsinki evacuated

indicators.note: of says the answer is taken from part of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Finland's capital has been cleared of its people.
explanation.walkthrough: The city sits across the end of 'Helsinki' and the start of 'evacuated'; Helsinki itself is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Ukraine, in its older spelling, is a major European city.

clue.text: Cut bits from dried fruit

definitions.meaning: to trim away parts, as a gardener does with a shrub

explanation.surface: Someone snips pieces off a piece of dried fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the verb for trimming branches and the name of a dried plum.

clue.text: Has boil, festering, to get rid of

indicators.note: festering suggests the letters are going bad and changing form

explanation.surface: A person with a festering boil must get rid of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To do away with something entirely, such as a law or custom, is a synonym of get rid of.

clue.text: Little Henry travelling to Farnham for running event

parts.note: Hal is the pet form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal

indicators.note: travelling says these letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A small boy called Henry is on his way to Farnham, a town in Surrey, for a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' means a short form of the name, not a small person.
explanation.definitionFit: A road race of about thirteen miles, half the full Olympic distance, is a running event.

clue.text: Insult coming from a van overheard

indicators.note: overheard says the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: the van is the front of an army, so a van gives a front

explanation.surface: An offensive remark comes from someone in a van, caught by a passer-by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' is short for vanguard, the leading part of a force.
explanation.definitionFit: An open slight or offence to someone's dignity is a synonym of insult.

clue.text: Retreating molten rock close to stern of ships

indicators.note: close to the stern means its very end, so its final letter
retreating means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: lava is molten rock from a volcano

explanation.surface: Molten lava flows back near the stern of some ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern' seems to belong to the ships, but only its last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describing a navy and its vessels means relating to ships.

clue.text: Piano disposed of kindly for rock band

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

indicators.note: disposed means arranged, so these letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: A piano is kindly given away for a rock band to use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed of' reads as one phrase, but 'of' is part of the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The British group behind The Dark Side of the Moon is a famous progressive rock band.

clue.text: Uninteresting people in Derby, for example

parts.note: flat means dull and lifeless
a race is a people sharing descent

explanation.surface: Dull people live in the city of Derby, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby looks like the English city, but here it is the Epsom horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derby is a horse race run on level ground with no jumps, an example of this kind of contest.

clue.text: Pickle: or something sweeter

definitions.meaning: a pickle is a predicament or tight spot
a fruit preserve, sweeter than a pickle

explanation.surface: Someone choosing between a sour relish and something sugary on the table.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a fix one is in and a sweet fruit spread.

clue.text: Make return flight around nightfall, finally: very dark

indicators.note: around puts the flight phrase on both sides of the picked letter

parts.note: to jet back is to fly home again

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word nightfall

explanation.surface: A traveller flies home around dusk, when it is very dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal-coloured, the deepest black, describes something extremely dark.

clue.text: One's going to … — well, no!

definitions.meaning: the contraction of I will, said of what one intends
the opposite of being well, that is unwell

explanation.surface: Someone starts to announce a plan, then breaks off and refuses.
explanation.definitionFit: Read with an apostrophe it is I will; plain, it means sick, not healthy.

clue.text: Reptile unsettled a girl a lot

indicators.note: unsettled says the letters are disturbed into another order

explanation.surface: A reptile greatly disturbed a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A large American crocodilian, which is a kind of reptile.

clue.text: Computer needing circuit: the best

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a track
top means the very best

explanation.surface: A computer needs a circuit board to be the best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circuit' suggests electronics, but here it is one round of a racetrack.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable machine used on the knees is a kind of computer.

clue.text: Keep a tugboat, for example

definitions.meaning: a keep is the fortified central stronghold of a castle
a tug is something that tows other vessels

explanation.surface: Someone advises holding on to a tugboat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb but is the noun for a castle stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle keep is a fortified stronghold, and a tug is one that hauls boats along.

clue.text: Other half of famous poem we devoured

indicators.note: devoured means swallowed, so the poem goes inside the pronoun

parts.note: If is Rudyard Kipling's famous poem

explanation.surface: Our other half from a well-known poem was eaten up by us.
explanation.definitionFit: Other half is an informal term for one's spouse or partner, the married woman here.

clue.text: Sport permitted little drama

parts.note: to sport is to play
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Games were allowed, causing a minor fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: The diminutive suffix makes a short stage piece, a small drama.

clue.text: Vault artist raised over church

indicators.note: over places the first piece above the church in a down entry
in a down clue, raised means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter is lifted over a church roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vault' suggests a leap, but it is the curved roof structure.
explanation.definitionFit: A vault is a curved roof, built as an extended form of this structure.

clue.text: In retro Aldershot cafe, decor is effective

indicators.note: retro says the hidden letters are read backwards
In says the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A café in Aldershot, a Hampshire army town, has decor in a retro style that works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals the letters sit inside the words; 'retro' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in fact or in practice, as something operative though not official.

clue.text: Chocolate producer approximately doubled output initially

indicators.note: doubled says the abbreviation is written twice

parts.note: ca is circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word output

explanation.surface: A cocoa grower roughly doubled production at first.
explanation.definitionFit: The tree whose beans are processed into chocolate produces it.
